key_errors: Failed to download the model: Server returned status code 503..

UnhandledPromiseRejection: This error originated either by throwing inside of an async function without a catch block, or by rejecting a promise which was not handled with .catch(). The promise rejected with the reason "Server returned status code 503.".
root_cause: The `npm run test_setup` step for the OpenVINO JS API tests downloads test fixture models from `raw.githubusercontent.com/openvinotoolkit/testdata`. All three parallel shards of the JS API job hit an identical `Server returned status code 503` from that GitHub-hosted raw-content endpoint while fetching `test_model_fp32.xml`, an unhandled promise rejection then crashes `tests/setup.js` with exit code 1 before any actual JS API test runs. Nothing in the PR's changed files (CPU/ARM ACL executor and FC weight-format code) touches the JS bindings, npm scripts, or test fixtures, so this is an external GitHub raw-content availability blip, not a regression introduced by the PR.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally - depends on transient 503 responses from raw.githubusercontent.com at fetch time. To attempt reproduction: cd src/bindings/js/node && npm run test_setup (may succeed once the upstream 503 clears).
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed OpenVINO JS API jobs; a plain retry very likely succeeds once GitHub's raw-content CDN clears the 503.
Consider adding retry/backoff logic around the model download in src/bindings/js/node/tests/setup.js so a single transient 503 doesn't fail the whole test_setup step.
Consider caching the testdata fixture files (e.g., via actions/cache) so JS API jobs don't repeatedly re-download the same static model files on every merge-queue run.
prevention_strategies: Add exponential-backoff retry (e.g., 2-3 attempts) around the HTTP fetch in tests/setup.js for downloading testdata fixtures, and surface a clearer error distinguishing infra/network failures from real test failures. Caching the small, rarely-changing test_model_fp32.xml/.bin fixtures would also remove the network dependency entirely from most runs.
historical_context: No prior CI Doctor MQ pattern was found for this specific 503-on-testdata-download signature; this is the first recorded occurrence in the merge-queue pattern database.
